title: Comparing Fractions with Same Numerator
objective: Compare fractions with the same numerator pictorially.
key_concept: When fractions have the same numerator, the one with the SMALLER denominator is LARGER (bigger pieces).

problems.text: Shade the models to compare the fractions. Circle the larger fraction.

answer.reason: Thirds are bigger pieces than fifths

problems.text: Shade the models to compare the fractions. Circle the larger fraction.

answer.reason: Eighths are bigger pieces than tenths

problems.text: Shade the models to compare the fractions. Circle the larger fraction.

answer.reason: Fourths are bigger pieces than eighths

problems.text: Shade the models to compare the fractions. Circle the larger fraction.

answer.reason: Sixths are bigger pieces than eighths

problems.text: Shade the models to compare the fractions. Circle the larger fraction.

After softball, Leslie and Kelly each buy a half-liter bottle of water. Leslie drinks 3 fourths of her water. Kelly drinks 3 fifths of her water. Who drinks the least amount of water? Draw a picture to support your answer.

answer.reason: 3/5 < 3/4 because fifths are smaller pieces than fourths

problems.text: Becky and Malory get matching piggy banks. Becky fills 2/3 of her piggy bank with pennies. Malory fills 2/4 of her piggy bank with pennies. Whose piggy bank has more pennies? Draw a picture to support your answer.

answer.reason: 2/3 > 2/4 because thirds are bigger pieces than fourths

problems.text: Heidi lines up her dolls in order from shortest to tallest. Doll A is 2/4 foot tall, Doll B is 2/6 foot tall, and Doll C is 2/3 foot tall. Compare the heights of the dolls to show how Heidi puts them in order. Draw a picture to support your answer.

answer.reason: Same numerator (2), so smaller denominator = larger fraction
